title: The Bell at the Bike Shop
blurb: The Bell at the Bike Shop
summary: Eva prueba dos timbres para su bicicleta.
text: Eva is at a bike shop. Her bike has no bell. The shop has a big bell and a small bell. Eva tries the big bell first. It is very loud. Bruno lifts his head. Then Eva tries the small bell. She can hear it, but Bruno stays on his mat. Eva buys the small bell. The shopkeeper puts it on her bike. Eva pays and walks home with Bruno.

comprehension_questions.question: What does Eva need for her bike?
What does Bruno do when the big bell rings?
comprehension_questions.explanation: Bruno levanta la cabeza al oír el timbre grande.

title: The Clock in the Window
text: A clock in a shop window showed half past four, but Eva's phone said five. She had promised to meet Leo outside the library at five fifteen. Rather than assume her phone was wrong, she asked the shopkeeper. He explained that the window clock was for sale and had stopped that morning. Eva had fifteen minutes left. She walked straight to the library instead of stopping for a snack. Leo arrived just as she reached the door. On their way home, they passed the shop again. The clock still showed half past four, but there was now a little sign beside it: batteries not included.

comprehension_questions.question: Why did the two times differ?
comprehension_questions.explanation: El reloj del escaparate se había detenido.

comprehension_questions.question: What does the final sign explain?
options: The buyer needs to supply batteries

title: The Parcel with Two Numbers
text: Eva offered to collect a parcel for her neighbour. The message showed number 18, but the label in the photo showed 81. Both buildings were on the same street, so she could not tell which number was right. At number 18, the receptionist said the shop used collection codes and did not need a home address. Eva realised she had confused the collection address with the delivery address printed on the label. Before showing the code, she called her neighbour to confirm which shop had sent the message. Once he confirmed it, she collected the parcel and sent him a short note explaining where the confusion had come from. The two numbers were both correct; they simply referred to different stages of the delivery.

comprehension_questions.question: Why were both numbers correct?
comprehension_questions.explanation: Uno indicaba la recogida y el otro la entrega.

comprehension_questions.question: Why did Eva call her neighbour?
options: To confirm the shop before sharing the code
comprehension_questions.explanation: Confirmó quién había enviado el mensaje antes de mostrar el código.

comprehension_questions.question: What resolved the confusion?
options: Understanding the purpose of each address
comprehension_questions.explanation: El problema era interpretar qué indicaba cada dirección.

title: One Microphone, Two Queues
text: At a community debate, the chair invited everyone to queue for the microphone. The arrangement seemed fair until Eva noticed that several participants could not stand for long. The chair considered letting them jump the queue, but that would require them to explain personal circumstances in public. Instead, volunteers began handing numbered cards to anyone who wanted to speak, whether seated or standing. An assistant carried the microphone to each person. The change solved one problem but revealed another: a few confident speakers took several turns before others had their first. The chair therefore introduced a second round for repeat contributions. Both changes preserved the order of requests within each round. After the meeting, the organisers compared who had actually spoken with who had asked to speak. They wanted to know whether the procedure worked in practice, not merely whether it looked orderly.

comprehension_questions.question: What did numbered cards achieve?
options: They removed the need to stand in line
comprehension_questions.explanation: Se podía pedir turno sin permanecer de pie.

comprehension_questions.question: Why add a second round?
comprehension_questions.explanation: Quienes aún no habían hablado obtuvieron prioridad.

comprehension_questions.question: What did the organisers compare?
options: The lengths of the two queues
The chair's notes and the agenda
Requests to speak and actual participation
comprehension_questions.explanation: Así podían evaluar si el sistema funcionaba.

title: The Promise in the Footnote
text: A museum described its new archive as permanently available to the public. An archivist pointed to a footnote: the museum would maintain access only while its licensing agreement remained in force. The communications team argued that the qualification was technically visible. Eva agreed that it was visible, but questioned whether a reader would reconcile it with the promise in the headline. A disclaimer can specify a minor exception; here, it withdrew the very certainty that made the announcement attractive. The team replaced the promise with a statement that the archive was available under the current agreement and that renewal would be reviewed annually. Some colleagues worried that the revised wording sounded less ambitious. Eva suggested that the ambition could still be stated separately: the museum intended to maintain access and was negotiating for a longer agreement. That distinction let the institution express commitment without presenting an outcome it could not yet guarantee.

comprehension_questions.question: What made the footnote inadequate?
options: It was missing from the page
It undermined the headline's central certainty
comprehension_questions.explanation: La nota anulaba la certeza que daba fuerza a la promesa.

comprehension_questions.question: What distinction does Eva preserve?
comprehension_questions.explanation: La institución podía manifestar una intención sin garantizarla.

comprehension_questions.question: What does 'technically visible' concede?
options: The caveat appeared, but might not correct the impression
comprehension_questions.explanation: Que se pueda ver no asegura que el lector corrija la impresión.

title: The Right to Leave a Blank
blurb: The Right to Leave a Blank
summary: The Right to Leave a Blank
text: A research team digitising a neighbourhood survey debated what to do with unanswered questions. One analyst wanted to infer likely replies from nearby entries, arguing that a complete dataset would make the district easier to compare with others. Another pointed out that silence had several possible sources: uncertainty, fatigue, distrust, or a deliberate refusal to answer. Treating all four as a statistical inconvenience would leave the apparent precision of the final report untouched while changing whose judgements it contained. Eva proposed retaining blanks and publishing separate estimates where comparisons genuinely required them. The report would describe the assumptions and show how different plausible interpretations affected the outcome. A colleague objected that this made the findings less decisive. Eva thought the decisiveness had been borrowed from an assumption that readers had never been invited to inspect. Still, her proposal did not make silence transparent. A blank left unfilled could mark a refusal, or simply a form put down in a hurry. What the team could preserve was the uncertainty, along with the possibility that some respondents had meant precisely to withhold a judgement.

comprehension_questions.question: What does 'borrowed' imply about decisiveness?
options: It was copied from another survey
It depended on a concealed assumption
It was guaranteed by sample size
comprehension_questions.explanation: La seguridad aparente provenía de un supuesto no expuesto.

comprehension_questions.question: Why publish estimates separately?
options: To distinguish modelling from observed replies
comprehension_questions.explanation: Se separa lo estimado de lo que las personas respondieron.

comprehension_questions.question: What limit does the conclusion acknowledge?
options: A blank is always a refusal
The reason for a particular blank remains unknown
comprehension_questions.explanation: Conservar un vacío no revela por qué quedó vacío.
